newsitem.title: USA: IES holders approve Interstate merger.
newsitem.headline: IES holders approve Interstate merger.

text.p: IES Industries Inc. said Thursday its shareholders voted to approve the proposed three-way merger with WPL Holdings Inc. and Interstate Power Corp. to form Interstate Energy Corp.
Shareholders appeared to have rejected a $1.17 billion bid for IES made last month by MidAmerican Energy Co.

Under terms of the merger agreement accepted Thursday, each IES share would be exchanged for 1.14 shares of the new company, each Interstate Power share would be exchanged for 1.11 share of the new company and each WPL share would be exchanged on a one-for-one basis.
Based on prices at midday Thursday, each IES share would be worth $33.63 and each Interstate share would be worth $32.75.
IES shares were trading Thursday at $32.25, down 87.5 cents; Interstate was trading at $30.75, unchanged, WPL shares were trading at $29.50, unchanged, all on the New York Stock Exchange.
MidAmerican Energy had offered IES shareholders a combination of stock and cash equivalent to $39 a share.
In a telephone news conference, MidAmerican refused to concede defeat in its attempt to take over IES.
"We're not conceding that as the outcome," said MidAmerican Chief Executive Stanley Bright. "The outcome cannot be known until a final tally is completed and we will await that," he said.
IES said more than 75 percent of IES shareholders voting, or more than 57 percent of shares outstanding, supported the merger.
IES also said the three-way merger was approved by the shareholders of WPL and Interstate Power at their respective shareholder meetings Thursday.
"Given the progress we have already made, we expect to proceed with the remaining regulatory reviews and to close this merger in the next eight to ten months," IES Chief Executive Lee Liu said.

IES in an electric utility holding company based in Cedar Rapids, Iowa. Interstate Power, based in Dubuque, Iowa, provides electrical and natural gas services in Minnesota, Iowa and Illinois. WPL Holdings, based in Madison, Wis., provides Electrical, gas and water services in southern and central Wisconsin.
"Interstate Energy Corporation will be a regional utility powerhouse, well positioned for the coming era of increased competition in our industry," said Lee Liu.
